title: California RV Insurance: What the Law Requires for Motorhomes and Trailers, and the Coverage Owners Actually Need
description: California RV insurance explained: 30/60/15 for motorhomes, no mandate for trailers, full-timer coverage, wildfire and storage risks, and typical costs.
author: Insurance Bhaiya Research Desk
keyTakeaways: Motorhomes (Class A, B and C) must carry California's standard 30/60/15 liability minimum, the same as a passenger car.

Travel trailers and fifth wheels have no stand-alone insurance mandate. Your tow vehicle's liability usually extends to the trailer while hitched, but nothing covers damage to the trailer itself unless you buy it.
If your RV is financed, the lender will require comprehensive and collision coverage.
Full-time RVers need full-timer coverage, which adds home-style personal liability and medical payments; a regular RV policy is built for vacation use.
Progressive reported average 2024 premiums among its customers of about $934 a year for motorhomes and $405 for travel trailers; your price depends heavily on RV value and usage.

faqs.question: Is RV insurance required in California?
faqs.answer: For motorhomes, yes: they must carry 30/60/15 liability like any car. Travel trailers and fifth wheels have no stand-alone requirement, though lenders require physical damage coverage on financed trailers.

faqs.question: Does my car insurance cover my travel trailer?
faqs.answer: Usually only the liability while the trailer is hitched to your insured vehicle. It does not cover damage to the trailer, its contents, or liability once it is unhitched. A separate trailer policy fills those gaps.

faqs.question: Do full-time RVers need special insurance in California?
faqs.answer: Yes. Full-timer coverage adds personal liability and medical payments similar to a homeowners policy. A vacation-use RV policy may not respond if the insurer learns the RV is your only residence.

faqs.question: How much is RV insurance in California?
faqs.answer: It varies widely by RV value and usage. Progressive reported 2024 averages among its customers of about $934 a year for motorhomes and $405 for travel trailers. Compare California's broader requirements in our [state auto insurance compliance guide](/learn/state-auto-insurance-compliance-guide/).

content.text: An RV is two risks in one: a vehicle that can cause a highway crash and a small home that can burn, flood or be burglarized at a campsite. California law only cares about the first risk, and only for RVs with an engine. Everything else, from the value of the RV to the liability when a guest trips on your folding steps, is up to you. This spoke of our [state auto insurance compliance guide](/learn/state-auto-insurance-compliance-guide/) sorts out what is mandatory, what is wise, and what is a waste for California owners.
What California Requires, by RV Type

rows: RV policy with liability; physical damage optional unless financed
RV policy or, for some converted vans, an auto policy
Tow vehicle's liability while hitched; separate trailer policy for physical damage
Truck auto policy plus an endorsement or separate policy for the camper unit

content.text: The motorhome minimum is the same 30/60/15 floor that applies to every California vehicle, and you must be able to show evidence of it on demand. If you aren't sure what counts as proof, see [California evidence of liability insurance](/learn/california-evidence-of-liability-insurance/).

content.title: The Unhitched Trailer Gap
content.text: Your auto policy's liability usually follows a trailer while it is attached. Once you unhitch at the campsite, that extension generally ends, and it never paid for damage to the trailer itself. A falling branch, a fire or a theft at the campground is only covered if you bought comprehensive coverage on the trailer. More in [does car insurance cover a travel trailer](/qa/does-car-insurance-cover-travel-trailer/).
Coverage California RV Owners Should Actually Consider

items: **Higher liability limits.** A 30,000-pound motorhome does far more damage than a sedan. Most RV owners carry at least 100/300/100, and many add an [umbrella policy](/learn/umbrella-insurance-guide/) on top.

**Comprehensive and collision.** Required by lenders; strongly advised for any RV you couldn't replace from savings. See [comprehensive vs collision](/compare/comprehensive-vs-collision/) for what each pays.

**Total loss replacement or agreed value.** Standard [actual cash value](/glossary/actual-cash-value/) settlements deduct depreciation, which is steep on RVs. Replacement or agreed-value options pay closer to what it costs to get back on the road.
**Vacation liability.** Covers injuries to others around your parked RV, such as a guest tripping over an awning stake.
**Personal effects.** Covers belongings inside the RV. Your homeowners policy may cover some items away from home, but often with lower limits.
**Emergency expense.** Pays lodging and transport if a breakdown or covered loss strands you far from home.
**Roadside assistance built for RVs.** A standard car tow truck cannot move a Class A; RV-specific roadside coverage is worth its small cost.

content.text: Full-Time RVers: The Policy Most People Skip

If the RV is your primary residence, a vacation-use RV policy leaves gaps a homeowners policy would normally fill. Full-timer coverage adds personal liability and medical payments that apply wherever you are, not just around the vehicle. Insurers will ask whether you own or rent a fixed home; answer honestly, because an undisclosed full-time use can lead to a denied claim. Our [8-Point Policy Check](/policy-check/) helps confirm you aren't relying on a homeowners policy you no longer have, and our [full-time RV insurance](/learn/full-time-rv-insurance/) guide covers domicile and coverage choices in depth.

items: **Wildfire.** Fire is a comprehensive peril. An RV stored in a fire-prone area with liability-only coverage gets nothing if it burns.
**Storage and lay-up.** Many insurers offer reduced premiums for months the RV is stored. Keep comprehensive active during storage; theft and fire don't take winters off.
**Towing rules.** California limits vehicles towing a trailer to 55 mph. Speed-related claims while towing can be contested.

**Interstate travelers.** Out-of-state RVs driving through California still need liability that meets California's floor while here. Florida snowbirds should compare their home-state requirements in our [Florida compliant drivers program](/learn/florida-compliant-drivers-program/) guide.

content.text: Progressive reported average 2024 [premiums](/glossary/premium/) among its own customers of about $934 a year for motorhomes and $405 for travel trailers, with liability-only motorhome policies starting much lower. Your price will be driven by the RV's value, class, how many months a year you use it, whether you live in it, your driving record and your chosen [deductible](/glossary/deductible/). A driver with a DUI-related filing will pay far more; see [SR-22 vs FR-44](/qa/sr22-vs-fr44-difference/) for how those filings interact with any vehicle you insure, including an RV.

content.title: Bundle, But Compare
content.text: Insuring the RV with the same company as your car and home usually earns a multi-policy discount. If you are buying a house at the same time, note that the lender's private mortgage insurance is a separate bill that bundling won't touch; see [California private mortgage insurance](/learn/california-private-mortgage-insurance/).
